html:
SMTO-HTTP-0027 — The files are too large to upload in one request

GUID: f687720f-3c69-4548-8c06-47f03add6adb
Slug: http-upload-limit
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO can upload only about 8 MB in one web request, counting the files and any form details sent with them. This upload was larger than that, so nothing was uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to upload the files one at a time, or in groups that add up to well under 8 MB. The limit applies to each request and includes form details sent with the files, so smaller groups fit.
  2. If one file is over 8 MB, make a smaller version (for example, compress it), add it with Add files to conversation, and ask SMTO to upload that. A file larger than the limit can't be sent in one request, and SMTO never cuts files short.
  3. Check on the web service which files arrived before asking SMTO to send the rest. Files sent in earlier requests may already be there, and sending them again could create duplicates.

What success looks like

  • Each smaller upload succeeds and SMTO shows the service's reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete earlier results or files from the conversation to make room; that doesn't change the upload limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP upload exceeds its size bound: the files total more than 8 MiB, or the encoded multipart body (files plus form fields) exceeds 8 MiB plus 64 KiB.

What this means

  • Upload source totals exceed 8 MiB, or encoded multipart output exceeds 8 MiB plus 65,536 bytes of envelope allowance. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Upload source totals exceed 8 MiB, or encoded multipart output exceeds 8 MiB plus 65,536 bytes of envelope allowance.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect total source bytes and multipart overhead separately; source-binding failures may be reported by the context boundary instead.

How to fix it

  • gateway_core/http_files.prepare_upload raises this when the encoded multipart body exceeds 8 MiB + 65,536 bytes; skills/http/files.upload_sources also raises it for sources over 8 MiB, but that path is currently re-mapped to http_context_unavailable, and the Gateway reports an aggregate over 8 MiB as http_upload_invalid. Reduce or batch uploads (and large form fields) to fit those limits without truncation.
  • Reduce or batch uploads to fit the advertised upload limits without truncation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A provider-supported smaller upload fits both source and encoded envelope bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
